---
title: "AMEP: Adult Migrant English Program"
description: "Information about participants in the Adult Migrant English Program, a free service to help eligible migrants improve their English language skills."
---

Information about participants in the Adult Migrant English Program, a free service to help eligible migrants improve their English language skills.

*Explains program eligibility, tuition services and the population represented by AMEP data.*

The classification behind it is the program's own split by delivery type, so the hours for 1 July 2018 to 30 September 2018 sit in AMEP_2018_Q3 for classroom tuition, in this column for distance learning, and in SPP_2018_Q3, SPPDL_2018_Q3, SLPT_2018_Q3, HTS_2018_Q3, EXTEND_2018_Q3 and CHILDCARE_2018_Q3 for the remaining types; EXTEND is the one hour type that starts only at 2017 Quarter 3, so it exists for this quarter but not for the earlier ones.","p":"2011 to 2019","s":"sourced","src":"Australian Council of TESOL Associations, ACTA Response to Home Affairs: Improving the AMEP, December 2019","url":"https://tesol.org.au/wp-content/uploads/2020/06/ACTA-RESPONSE-TO-HOME-AFFAIRS-Improving-the-AMEP-December-2019.pdf","lim":"It is not remaining entitlement. The break at 1 July 2017 also means a level shift in this column is a contracting change first and a behavioural change second.","where":["madipge-mig-d-amep-activity-11-19 / amep_clientshours_2011_19"]},{"n":"AMEPDL_2018_Q4","d":"Hours of Adult Migrant English Program distance learning tuition a client attended in Quarter 4 of 2018.","full":"Hours of Adult Migrant English Program distance learning tuition a client attended in Quarter 4 of 2018. It is one column of the quarterly panel that runs from 2011 Quarter 3 to 2019 Quarter 2 in amep_clientshours_2011_19, so a person's series runs across the columns of one row and not down rows. It is the thirtieth of the 32 quarterly columns, covering October to December 2018, the second quarter of the 2018-19 financial year and the sixth quarter under the contract that began on 1 July 2017. The Australian Council of TESOL Associations, reporting the department's own evaluation, records that \"The transition to the new contract, however, saw a dramatic 80 per cent decrease in DL commencements\", so the level of this column is not comparable with the same quarter before 2017.","dsrc":"Australian Council of TESOL Associations, ACTA Response to Home Affairs: Improving the AMEP, December 2019","durl":"https://tesol.org.au/wp-content/uploads/2020/06/ACTA-RESPONSE-TO-HOME-AFFAIRS-Improving-the-AMEP-December-2019.pdf","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"AMEPDL (510 hour entitlement) - number of hours attended by client in 2018 Quarter 4","k":"Distance learning tuition hours attended in 2018 Quarter 4","def":"A count of tuition hours attended in the period, non-negative and reported to the hour, laid out one column per period rather than one row per period. The classification behind it is the program's own split by delivery type, so the hours for 1 October 2018 to 31 December 2018 sit in AMEP_2018_Q4 for classroom tuition, in this column for distance learning, and in SPP_2018_Q4, SPPDL_2018_Q4, SLPT_2018_Q4, HTS_2018_Q4, EXTEND_2018_Q4 and CHILDCARE_2018_Q4 for the remaining types; EXTEND is the one hour type that starts only at 2017 Quarter 3, so it exists for this quarter but not for the earlier ones.","p":"2011 to 2019","s":"sourced","src":"Australian Council of TESOL Associations, ACTA Response to Home Affairs: Improving the AMEP, December 2019","url":"https://tesol.org.au/wp-content/uploads/2020/06/ACTA-RESPONSE-TO-HOME-AFFAIRS-Improving-the-AMEP-December-2019.pdf","lim":"The quarter is a reporting bucket, not a course. The break at 1 July 2017 also means a level shift in this column is a contracting change first and a behavioural change second.","where":["madipge-mig-d-amep-activity-11-19 / amep_clientshours_2011_19"]},{"n":"AMEPDL_2019_Q1","d":"Hours of Adult Migrant English Program distance learning tuition a client attended in Quarter 1 of 2019.","full":"Hours of Adult Migrant English Program distance learning tuition a client attended in Quarter 1 of 2019. It is one column of the quarterly panel that runs from 2011 Quarter 3 to 2019 Quarter 2 in amep_clientshours_2011_19, so a person's series runs across the columns of one row and not down rows. It is the thirty-first of the 32 quarterly columns, covering January to March 2019, the third quarter of the 2018-19 financial year and the seventh quarter under the contract that began on 1 July 2017. The Australian Council of TESOL Associations, reporting the department's own evaluation, records that \"The transition to the new contract, however, saw a dramatic 80 per cent decrease in DL commencements\", so the level of this column is not comparable with the same quarter before 2017.","dsrc":"Australian Council of TESOL Associations, ACTA Response to Home Affairs: Improving the AMEP, December 2019","durl":"https://tesol.org.au/wp-content/uploads/2020/06/ACTA-RESPONSE-TO-HOME-AFFAIRS-Improving-the-AMEP-December-2019.pdf","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"AMEPDL (510 hour entitlement) - number of hours attended by client in 2019 Quarter 1","k":"Distance learning tuition hours attended in 2019 Quarter 1","def":"A count of tuition hours attended in the period, non-negative and reported to the hour, laid out one column per period rather than one row per period. The classification behind it is the program's own split by delivery type, so the hours for 1 January 2019 to 31 March 2019 sit in AMEP_2019_Q1 for classroom tuition, in this column for distance learning, and in SPP_2019_Q1, SPPDL_2019_Q1, SLPT_2019_Q1, HTS_2019_Q1, EXTEND_2019_Q1 and CHILDCARE_2019_Q1 for the remaining types; EXTEND is the one hour type that starts only at 2017 Quarter 3, so it exists for this quarter but not for the earlier ones.","p":"2011 to 2019","s":"sourced","src":"Australian Council of TESOL Associations, ACTA Response to Home Affairs: Improving the AMEP, December 2019","url":"https://tesol.org.au/wp-content/uploads/2020/06/ACTA-RESPONSE-TO-HOME-AFFAIRS-Improving-the-AMEP-December-2019.pdf","lim":"The count is hours attended, not hours offered or enrolled for, so a drop from the quarter before into 2019 Quarter 1 can be a provider changing how it refers clients to distance learning rather than a client studying less. The break at 1 July 2017 also means a level shift in this column is a contracting change first and a behavioural change second.","where":["madipge-mig-d-amep-activity-11-19 / amep_clientshours_2011_19"]},{"n":"AMEPDL_2019_Q2","d":"Hours of Adult Migrant English Program distance learning tuition a client attended in Quarter 2 of 2019.","full":"Hours of Adult Migrant English Program distance learning tuition a client attended in Quarter 2 of 2019. It is one column of the quarterly panel that runs from 2011 Quarter 3 to 2019 Quarter 2 in amep_clientshours_2011_19, so a person's series runs across the columns of one row and not down rows. It is the last of the 32 quarterly columns, covering April to June 2019, the final quarter of the 2018-19 financial year and the eighth quarter under the contract that began on 1 July 2017; a client still studying at 30 June 2019 simply runs off the end of the table. The Australian Council of TESOL Associations, reporting the department's own evaluation, records that \"The transition to the new contract, however, saw a dramatic 80 per cent decrease in DL commencements\", so the level of this column is not comparable with the same quarter before 2017.","dsrc":"Australian Council of TESOL Associations, ACTA Response to Home Affairs: Improving the AMEP, December 2019","durl":"https://tesol.org.au/wp-content/uploads/2020/06/ACTA-RESPONSE-TO-HOME-AFFAIRS-Improving-the-AMEP-December-2019.pdf","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"AMEPDL (510 hour entitlement) - number of hours attended by client in 2019 Quarter 2","k":"Distance learning tuition hours attended in 2019 Quarter 2","def":"A count of tuition hours attended in the period, non-negative and reported to the hour, laid out one column per period rather than one row per period. The classification behind it is the program's own split by delivery type, so the hours for 1 April 2019 to 30 June 2019 sit in AMEP_2019_Q2 for classroom tuition, in this column for distance learning, and in SPP_2019_Q2, SPPDL_2019_Q2, SLPT_2019_Q2, HTS_2019_Q2, EXTEND_2019_Q2 and CHILDCARE_2019_Q2 for the remaining types; EXTEND is the one hour type that starts only at 2017 Quarter 3, so it exists for this quarter but not for the earlier ones.","p":"2011 to 2019","s":"sourced","src":"Australian Council of TESOL Associations, ACTA Response to Home Affairs: Improving the AMEP, December 2019","url":"https://tesol.org.au/wp-content/uploads/2020/06/ACTA-RESPONSE-TO-HOME-AFFAIRS-Improving-the-AMEP-December-2019.pdf","lim":"It is not remaining entitlement. The 510 hour entitlement named in the custodian's label carries extensions that the sources describe only as complex and overlapping, and the classroom hours in AMEP and the Special Preparatory Program hours in SPP and SPPDL sit in their own columns, so nothing in the table shows how much of a client's allowance the hours in 2019 Quarter 2 left. It is the final quarter in the table as well, so a client still studying at 30 June 2019 has a series that stops rather than a series that ends.","where":["madipge-mig-d-amep-activity-11-19 / amep_clientshours_2011_19"]},{"n":"AMET_CLNT_ID","d":"The client number the program's own case system gave this person, and the key that joins the six AMEP tables to each other.","full":"The client number the program's own case system gave this person, and the key that joins the six AMEP tables to each other. ARMS is the AMEP Reporting and Management System, described in the accreditation manual for the program as the source the department monitors outcomes from: \"NEAS does not monitor outcomes; these are directly monitored by DIAC through statistical data made available via the AMEP Reporting and Management System (ARMS).\" It therefore travels with registration, hours, English proficiency, CSWE awards and address for the same client, while SYNTHETIC_AEUID is the separate column that reaches the PLIDA spine.","dsrc":"National ELT Accreditation Scheme, Standards and Criteria for AMEP Accreditation 2009, hosted by the Australian Council of TESOL Associations","durl":"https://tesol.org.au/wp-content/uploads/2019/01/AMEP-Standards-Manual-2009.pdf","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"AMEP client ID generated in ARMS database unique identifier","k":"ARMS client identifier","def":"An opaque identifier minted in ARMS, one value per program client, with no published format and no meaning carried in its characters. It repeats for the same client across the hours, client profile, CSWE award, English proficiency and address tables, and appears in no other PLIDA dataset.","p":"2003 to 2011, 2003 to 2019, 2011 to 2019","s":"sourced","src":"National ELT Accreditation Scheme, Standards and Criteria for AMEP Accreditation 2009, hosted by the Australian Council of TESOL Associations","url":"https://tesol.org.au/wp-content/uploads/2019/01/AMEP-Standards-Manual-2009.pdf","lim":"It reaches nothing outside the program. A client's Centrelink, tax, Census or health records are found through SYNTHETIC_AEUID, not through this number, so it cannot be used as a person key for the asset. It is also not the only ARMS client number on the AMEP tables: amep_englishproficiency carries a second one, CLNT_ID, which the custodian describes as the identifier used to report competency achievements, so the two columns should not be joined as though they were interchangeable without first checking that they agree.","where":["madipge-mig-d-amep-activity-03-11 / amep_clientshours_2003_11","madipge-mig-d-amep-activity-11-19 / amep_clientshours_2011_19","madipge-mig-d-amep-address-03-19 / amep_address_2003_19","madipge-mig-d-amep-awards-03-19 / amep_csweawards","madipge-mig-d-amep-client-03-19 / amep_cltpro_dob_visa_treated","madipge-mig-d-amep-english-03-19 / amep_englishproficiency"]},{"n":"ARMS_FLAGGED_EXIT_DATE","d":"The day the program's case system, ARMS, recorded this client as having left the Adult Migrant English Program.","full":"The day the program's case system, ARMS, recorded this client as having left the Adult Migrant English Program. The word flagged is doing work: the exit is a status a provider or the system set in the AMEP Reporting and Management System, not an event the client reported. It sits beside ENTITLEMENT_END_DATE on the same client profile row, and the two answer different questions, one being when the department closed the client and the other being when the tuition entitlement lapses whether or not the client ever attended.","dsrc":"National ELT Accreditation Scheme, Standards and Criteria for AMEP Accreditation 2009, hosted by the Australian Council of TESOL Associations","durl":"https://tesol.org.au/wp-content/uploads/2019/01/AMEP-Standards-Manual-2009.pdf","dp":"ai","vp":"ai","od":"Date client exited from AMEP","k":"Date the case system flagged the client as exited from the program","def":"A calendar date with an open domain, bounded below by the earliest program registration in the collection and above by the extract day carried in DATE_EXTRACTED. One value per client, held on the client profile table rather than on an episode row.","p":"2003 to 2019","s":"sourced","src":"National ELT Accreditation Scheme, Standards and Criteria for AMEP Accreditation 2009, hosted by the Australian Council of TESOL Associations","url":"https://tesol.org.au/wp-content/uploads/2019/01/AMEP-Standards-Manual-2009.pdf","lim":"It does not date the end of study. A client who simply stops coming is flagged when the provider or the system gets to it, so the gap between the last quarter with hours in amep_clientshours_2011_19 and this date can run to several quarters. A client still on the books at extraction carries no date rather than a future one, so treating a missing value as censoring and a present value as an event will mix administrative tidying in with genuine exits.","where":["madipge-mig-d-amep-client-03-19 / amep_cltpro_dob_visa_treated"]},{"n":"ARMS_FLAGGED_EXIT_TYPE","d":"The reason category ARMS held for why this client left the Adult Migrant English Program.","full":"The reason category ARMS held for why this client left the Adult Migrant English Program. It pairs with ARMS_FLAGGED_EXIT_DATE, and together they are the only record on the asset of how a person's participation ended. The categories come from the AMEP Reporting and Management System that the department uses to monitor the program, so they are administrative reasons chosen by a provider, and the registry publishes no code list for them.","dsrc":"National ELT Accreditation Scheme, Standards and Criteria for AMEP Accreditation 2009, hosted by the Australian Council of TESOL Associations","durl":"https://tesol.org.au/wp-content/uploads/2019/01/AMEP-Standards-Manual-2009.pdf","dp":"ai","vp":"ai","od":"Reason client exited from AMEP - reason type","k":"Reason type recorded when a client was flagged as exited","def":"A short categorical code drawn from the exit reasons the case system offers a provider. The classification is the department's own operational one; it is not the Australian Core Skills Framework and not any national training classification.","p":"2003 to 2019","s":"sourced","src":"National ELT Accreditation Scheme, Standards and Criteria for AMEP Accreditation 2009, hosted by the Australian Council of TESOL Associations","url":"https://tesol.org.au/wp-content/uploads/2019/01/AMEP-Standards-Manual-2009.pdf","lim":"It is not an outcome. Using up the tuition entitlement, reaching the assessed level, moving interstate and never coming back are all exits, and this field will not separate a client who finished from one who gave up. It is also not the result of an exit assessment: the accreditation manual lists \"results of student exit assessments\" among the provider records that its panels do not normally examine, and those results never reach this table, so a proficiency outcome has to come from amep_englishproficiency instead.","where":["madipge-mig-d-amep-client-03-19 / amep_cltpro_dob_visa_treated"]},{"n":"AWARD_CODE","d":"The case system code for the Certificate in Spoken and Written English award or course this client was granted after assessment.","full":"The case system code for the Certificate in Spoken and Written English award or course this client was granted after assessment. It appears on both sides of a join: once per attainment in amep_csweawards, where it sits with AWARD_DATE and the client's ARMS number, and once per code in amep_csweawardsrefcodes, which turns it into AWARD_NAME, AWARD_DESCRIPTION, CSWE_LEVEL and CSWE_ACCREDITATION_YEAR. The certificates were the program's common curriculum, and the assessment behind an award was moderated, the accreditation manual requiring \"annual assessment moderation as required under CSWE licensing\" of every provider.","dsrc":"National ELT Accreditation Scheme, Standards and Criteria for AMEP Accreditation 2009, hosted by the Australian Council of TESOL Associations","durl":"https://tesol.org.au/wp-content/uploads/2019/01/AMEP-Standards-Manual-2009.pdf","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"ARMS code for CSWE award/course granted to client (following assessment)","k":"ARMS code for a Certificate in Spoken and Written English award or course","def":"A short code from a closed departmental list, resolvable only by joining amep_csweawardsrefcodes on the same column. The list is the case system's own course register, so the code should be resolved through that reference table rather than assumed to be a national training package course number.","p":"2003 to 2019","s":"sourced","src":"National ELT Accreditation Scheme, Standards and Criteria for AMEP Accreditation 2009, hosted by the Australian Council of TESOL Associations","url":"https://tesol.org.au/wp-content/uploads/2019/01/AMEP-Standards-Manual-2009.pdf","lim":"The code says which award, not how well and not at what level: CSWE_LEVEL in the reference table carries the certificate level and neither table records a mark. Absence is not failure either, because a client can attend for years without an award row, and from 1 July 2017 new clients were assessed against the Australian Core Skills Framework instead, which is recorded in amep_englishproficiency and never produces a code here.","where":["madipge-mig-d-amep-award-codes-03-19 / amep_csweawardsrefcodes","madipge-mig-d-amep-awards-03-19 / amep_csweawards"]},{"n":"AWARD_DATE","d":"The date a Certificate in Spoken and Written English award was granted to this client, which the custodian records as the date of the assessment.","full":"The date a Certificate in Spoken and Written English award was granted to this client, which the custodian records as the date of the assessment. There is one row per award in amep_csweawards, so a client with three certificates has three rows and a client with none has no row at all, and this is the only dated attainment anywhere on the AMEP tables. Assessment was a scheduled, moderated activity rather than a continuous one, the accreditation manual requiring that \"External (cross-provider) CSWE moderation should be undertaken at least annually, and teachers kept informed of the results of assessment moderation.\"","dsrc":"National ELT Accreditation Scheme, Standards and Criteria for AMEP Accreditation 2009, hosted by the Australian Council of TESOL Associations","durl":"https://tesol.org.au/wp-content/uploads/2019/01/AMEP-Standards-Manual-2009.pdf","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Date CSWE award/course granted to client (date of assessment)","k":"Date a Certificate in Spoken and Written English award was granted","def":"A calendar date with an open domain, bounded in practice by the program collection window that runs from 2003 to 2019. It dates the assessment that granted the award, not the enrolment, the course start or the course end.","p":"2003 to 2019","s":"sourced","src":"National ELT Accreditation Scheme, Standards and Criteria for AMEP Accreditation 2009, hosted by the Australian Council of TESOL Associations","url":"https://tesol.org.au/wp-content/uploads/2019/01/AMEP-Standards-Manual-2009.pdf","lim":"It cannot date the learning. A certificate assessed in one quarter can rest on hours attended across several, and because moderation is annual and cross-provider the dates cluster into assessment rounds, so the interval between this date and a rise in the hours columns is scheduling as much as progress. Award rows also thin out after 1 July 2017, when new clients moved to Australian Core Skills Framework assessment, so a falling count of awards after that date understates attainment rather than measuring a decline in it.","where":["madipge-mig-d-amep-awards-03-19 / amep_csweawards"]},{"n":"AWARD_DESCRIPTION","d":"The longer summary of a Certificate in Spoken and Written English award, held once per AWARD_CODE in the reference table amep_csweawardsrefcodes.","full":"The longer summary of a Certificate in Spoken and Written English award, held once per AWARD_CODE in the reference table amep_csweawardsrefcodes. It is the fuller companion to AWARD_NAME and, like it, describes a course rather than a person, so it reaches a client only through AWARD_CODE. The text is the department's own summary in the case system rather than the accredited course specification, and that specification changed when the certificates were re-accredited to Australian Skills Quality Authority requirements in 2018.","dsrc":"Australian Council of TESOL Associations, ACTA Response to Home Affairs: Improving the AMEP, December 2019","durl":"https://tesol.org.au/wp-content/uploads/2020/06/ACTA-RESPONSE-TO-HOME-AFFAIRS-Improving-the-AMEP-December-2019.pdf","dp":"ai","vp":"ai","od":"Description/summary of CSWE award/course","k":"Summary text for a Certificate in Spoken and Written English award or course","def":"Free text of variable length, one value per code, with no controlled vocabulary and no code list behind it. The structured facts about the same code sit in CSWE_LEVEL and CSWE_ACCREDITATION_YEAR.","p":"2003 to 2019","s":"sourced","src":"Australian Council of TESOL Associations, ACTA Response to Home Affairs: Improving the AMEP, December 2019","url":"https://tesol.org.au/wp-content/uploads/2020/06/ACTA-RESPONSE-TO-HOME-AFFAIRS-Improving-the-AMEP-December-2019.pdf","lim":"It is not a syllabus and not a competency list, so it cannot be used to say what the holder of an award can do in English. It is not stable evidence of content either: the reference table holds one description per code, so a summary written after a re-accreditation is applied to awards granted years before it, and comparing descriptions across codes will read curriculum drafting differences as differences in learning.","where":["madipge-mig-d-amep-award-codes-03-19 / amep_csweawardsrefcodes"]},{"n":"AWARD_NAME","d":"The title of the Certificate in Spoken and Written English course or award that an AWARD_CODE stands for.","full":"The title of the Certificate in Spoken and Written English course or award that an AWARD_CODE stands for. It lives in the reference table amep_csweawardsrefcodes, one row per code, so it describes a course and never a client, and the client side of the join is amep_csweawards. Reading it with CSWE_ACCREDITATION_YEAR matters, because the Australian Council of TESOL Associations records of the certificates that \"re-accreditation to meet ASQA requirements in 2018 has seriously impoverished and distorted it\", so a title does not carry the same content across the whole collection window.","dsrc":"Australian Council of TESOL Associations, ACTA Response to Home Affairs: Improving the AMEP, December 2019","durl":"https://tesol.org.au/wp-content/uploads/2020/06/ACTA-RESPONSE-TO-HOME-AFFAIRS-Improving-the-AMEP-December-2019.pdf","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Name/title of CSWE award/course","k":"Title of a Certificate in Spoken and Written English award or course","def":"Free text from the case system's course register, one string per AWARD_CODE, with no controlled vocabulary. The naming follows the Certificates in Spoken and Written English series, whose certificate levels are held separately in CSWE_LEVEL.","p":"2003 to 2019","s":"sourced","src":"Australian Council of TESOL Associations, ACTA Response to Home Affairs: Improving the AMEP, December 2019","url":"https://tesol.org.au/wp-content/uploads/2020/06/ACTA-RESPONSE-TO-HOME-AFFAIRS-Improving-the-AMEP-December-2019.pdf","lim":"A title is not a level and not a ranking. Two awards with similar names can sit at different certificate levels, and because the reference table gives a code no start or end date, the name cannot tell you which years the award was actually available to clients. It is also not a national qualification title, so it should not be matched by string against the national training register.","where":["madipge-mig-d-amep-award-codes-03-19 / amep_csweawardsrefcodes"]},{"n":"CHILD_CHILDCARE_CENTRE","d":"A coded pairing of each of a client's children with the childcare centre that child attended while the client studied.","full":"A coded pairing of each of a client's children with the childcare centre that child attended while the client studied. The Adult Migrant English Program funds childcare so that parents can attend tuition, and the accreditation manual sets where that care happens as a standard: \"Childcare locations are convenient to AMEP delivery locations or clients' homes.\" The column sits on the client profile table with CHILDCARE_REQUIRED, the count of children needing care, while the hours used are in the quarterly CHILDCARE columns of amep_clientshours_2011_19.","dsrc":"National ELT Accreditation Scheme, Standards and Criteria for AMEP Accreditation 2009, hosted by the Australian Council of TESOL Associations","durl":"https://tesol.org.au/wp-content/uploads/2019/01/AMEP-Standards-Manual-2009.pdf","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Client's child/ren (code) and the childcare centre the child/ren attended (code)","k":"Coded pairing of a client's child with the childcare centre attended","def":"A composite of two case system codes, one standing for the child and one for the centre, held on the client's profile row. Neither code resolves through a published list in this asset, and a client with several children carries several pairs in the one column.","p":"2003 to 2019","s":"sourced","src":"National ELT Accreditation Scheme, Standards and Criteria for AMEP Accreditation 2009, hosted by the Australian Council of TESOL Associations","url":"https://tesol.org.au/wp-content/uploads/2019/01/AMEP-Standards-Manual-2009.pdf","lim":"The child code is not a person on the PLIDA spine, so a child named here cannot be followed into Census, health or education records; only the parent links out, through SYNTHETIC_AEUID. The centre code is not an address or a service provider identifier either, so it cannot be geocoded or matched to childcare services recorded elsewhere in the asset, and because the column is undated it cannot say when a child moved between centres.","where":["madipge-mig-d-amep-client-03-19 / amep_cltpro_dob_visa_treated"]},{"n":"CHILDCARE_2011_Q3","d":"Hours of program-funded childcare used for an Adult Migrant English Program client's children in Quarter 3 of 2011.","full":"Hours of program-funded childcare used for an Adult Migrant English Program client's children in Quarter 3 of 2011. This is the first quarter of the childcare panel. The hours are recorded against the parent who is the client rather than against the child, and the column is one cell of the quarterly panel in amep_clientshours_2011_19 that runs to 2019 Quarter 2, so a family's series reads across a row. Childcare is a support service rather than tuition, and the accreditation manual for the program sets it as a standard in its own right: \"Childcare provision is appropriate to the needs of clients.\"","dsrc":"National ELT Accreditation Scheme, Standards and Criteria for AMEP Accreditation 2009, hosted by the Australian Council of TESOL Associations","durl":"https://tesol.org.au/wp-content/uploads/2019/01/AMEP-Standards-Manual-2009.pdf","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"CHILDCARE - number of hours attended by client in 2011 Quarter 3","k":"Program-funded childcare hours used in 2011 Quarter 3","def":"A count of care hours between 1 July 2011 and 30 September 2011, non-negative, sitting on the same client row as the tuition hour columns AMEP_2011_Q3, AMEPDL_2011_Q3, SPP_2011_Q3, SPPDL_2011_Q3, SLPT_2011_Q3 and HTS_2011_Q3; there is no EXTEND_2011_Q3, because that hour type starts only at 2017 Quarter 3. Childcare sits under support services in the 2009 accreditation standards rather than under program delivery, so these are service-use hours and not tuition hours; the sources do not say how, if at all, they bear on a client's tuition entitlement.","p":"2011 to 2019","s":"sourced","src":"National ELT Accreditation Scheme, Standards and Criteria for AMEP Accreditation 2009, hosted by the Australian Council of TESOL Associations","url":"https://tesol.org.au/wp-content/uploads/2019/01/AMEP-Standards-Manual-2009.pdf","lim":"It does not say how many children were cared for or which ones: CHILDCARE_REQUIRED holds the count and CHILD_CHILDCARE_CENTRE the child-to-centre pairing, and neither is dated. An empty cell is also ambiguous, since a client with no children, a client who arranged care privately and a person who was not enrolled that quarter all leave the same blank. Care used before July 2011 is not in this table at all, so a client who studied from 2008 and needed care throughout shows nothing here for the first three years and looks like a new user of childcare.","where":["madipge-mig-d-amep-activity-11-19 / amep_clientshours_2011_19"]},{"n":"CHILDCARE_2011_Q4","d":"Hours of program-funded childcare used for an Adult Migrant English Program client's children in Quarter 4 of 2011.","full":"Hours of program-funded childcare used for an Adult Migrant English Program client's children in Quarter 4 of 2011. This is the second quarter of the childcare panel and the last of 2011. The hours are recorded against the parent who is the client rather than against the child, and the column is one cell of the quarterly panel in amep_clientshours_2011_19 that runs to 2019 Quarter 2, so a family's series reads across a row. The table holds a client per row, so the quarter-by-quarter series is spread across columns and has to be pivoted before it behaves like a time series. Home Affairs says of the program that \"People attending face to face classes can access free childcare for children under school age.\"","dsrc":"Department of Home Affairs, Adult Migrant English Program","durl":"https://immi.homeaffairs.gov.au/settling-in-australia/amep","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"CHILDCARE - number of hours attended by client in 2019 Quarter 1","k":"Childcare hours attended in the March quarter 2019","def":"A non-negative number of hours of childcare, held one column per client per quarter, so the column is a count of hours and not a status or a code. This is the second year of the new business model and the last year the panel covers, so a client still in care after June 2019 simply runs off the end of the table. Column names run CHILDCARE_YYYY_Qn over calendar quarters, Q1 being January to March; the panel opens at 2011 Q3 and closes at 2019 Q2, which is eight financial years from 1 July 2011 to 30 June 2019.","p":"2011 to 2019","s":"sourced","src":"Department of Home Affairs, Evaluation of the Adult Migrant English Program New Business Model (Social Compass, 2019)","url":"https://immi.homeaffairs.gov.au/amep-subsite/Files/amep-evalution-new-business-model.pdf","lim":"The column names the quarter but not the provider or the arrangement, so onsite creche, a subcontracted centre and a centre chosen by the student are indistinguishable.","where":["madipge-mig-d-amep-activity-11-19 / amep_clientshours_2011_19"]},{"n":"CHILDCARE_REQUIRED","d":"The number of the client's children who need an AMEP childcare place, recorded once on the client profile rather than per quarter.","full":"The number of the client's children who need an AMEP childcare place, recorded once on the client profile rather than per quarter. Home Affairs states that \"People attending face to face classes can access free childcare for children under school age\", so the count is of pre-school children whose care would let the parent attend class. It is a stated requirement captured at the client record, which is why it sits beside CHILD_CHILDCARE_CENTRE, the field that names each child and the centre they attended.","dsrc":"Department of Home Affairs, Adult Migrant English Program","durl":"https://immi.homeaffairs.gov.au/settling-in-australia/amep","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Number of children who require childcare service","k":"Count of children needing AMEP childcare","def":"A small non-negative integer counting children. There is no classification behind it: the value is a headcount taken from the client's own record in the AMEP Reporting and Management System, not a code list.","p":"2003 to 2019","s":"sourced","src":"Department of Home Affairs, Adult Migrant English Program","url":"https://immi.homeaffairs.gov.au/settling-in-australia/amep","lim":"It is a requirement, not a placement. The system that issues it is the AMEP Reporting and Management System (ARMS), the provider-facing database in which service providers record attendance, progress and assessment. It is an administrative key of the program, not a PLIDA key: SYNTHETIC_AEUID is the column that links a client to the rest of the asset.","dsrc":"Department of Home Affairs, Evaluation of the Adult Migrant English Program New Business Model (Social Compass, 2019)","durl":"https://immi.homeaffairs.gov.au/amep-subsite/Files/amep-evalution-new-business-model.pdf","dp":"ai","vp":"ai","od":"AMEP client ID generated in ARMS database unique identifier - used to report competency achievements","k":"ARMS client identifier used for competency reporting","def":"An opaque provider-system identifier issued by ARMS. It has no classification behind it and carries no information about the person; its only job is to tie the ACSF and ASLPR assessment columns on this table back to one client.","p":"2003 to 2019","s":"sourced","src":"Department of Home Affairs, Evaluation of the Adult Migrant English Program New Business Model (Social Compass, 2019)","url":"https://immi.homeaffairs.gov.au/amep-subsite/Files/amep-evalution-new-business-model.pdf","lim":"Do not assume it equals AMET_CLNT_ID, which sits on the same row. The item list distinguishes them precisely because the competency reporting stream used its own client number, so joining assessment records on the wrong one silently drops clients.","where":["madipge-mig-d-amep-english-03-19 / amep_englishproficiency"]},{"n":"COUNTRY_OF_BIRTH","d":"The country the AMEP client was born in, as held on their client profile in the program's own records.","full":"The country the AMEP client was born in, as held on their client profile in the program's own records. The evaluation reports that AMEP students come from 197 countries and speak 267 languages, so the field is spread thinly across a very large number of categories. Country of birth in PLIDA is normally carried on the ABS Standard Australian Classification of Countries, which has 255 country categories grouped into 27 minor groups and nine major groups.","dsrc":"ABS, Standard Australian Classification of Countries (SACC), latest release","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/classifications/standard-australian-classification-countries-sacc/latest-release","dp":"ai","vp":"ai","od":"Client's birth country","k":"Country of birth of the AMEP client","def":"A country code or country name. Where the ABS classification applies, the base level is a four-digit country code such as 5101 Myanmar, aggregating to a two-digit minor group and a one-digit major group by geographic proximity.","p":"2003 to 2019","s":"sourced","src":"ABS, Standard Australian Classification of Countries (SACC), latest release","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/classifications/standard-australian-classification-countries-sacc/latest-release","lim":"Whether the codes on this column are ABS four-digit country codes or the department's own country list is not stated in the item list, so the codes should be checked in the environment before they are mapped; a mismatch shows up as a large residual rather than as an error.","where":["madipge-mig-d-amep-client-03-19 / amep_cltpro_dob_visa_treated"]},{"n":"CSWE_ACCREDITATION_YEAR","d":"The year a Certificates in Spoken and Written English course was accredited as a national VET course, held on the award reference table, not against a client.","full":"The year a Certificates in Spoken and Written English course was accredited as a national VET course, held on the award reference table, not against a client. The Australian Skills Quality Authority is the national VET regulator and says it \"accredits courses where a clearly demonstrated training need cannot be met through a nationally endorsed training package qualification\". The year therefore dates the version of the course, which is how two CSWE award codes with the same certificate name are told apart.","dsrc":"Australian Skills Quality Authority, Course accreditation","durl":"https://www.asqa.gov.au/for-providers/course-accreditation","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Year that CSWE award/course accredited by Australian Skills Quality Authority (ASQA) or equivalent","k":"Year the CSWE course was accredited as a VET accredited course","def":"A four-digit calendar year. It is an attribute of the course carried in the reference table, one row per AWARD_CODE, and is set by the accreditation decision rather than by anything the client did.","p":"2003 to 2019","s":"sourced","src":"Australian Skills Quality Authority, Course accreditation","url":"https://www.asqa.gov.au/for-providers/course-accreditation","lim":"It is not the year the client earned anything. AWARD_DATE on amep_csweawards is the date of the client's assessment, and the two can be many years apart because an accredited course stays current for its whole accreditation period.","where":["madipge-mig-d-amep-award-codes-03-19 / amep_csweawardsrefcodes"]},{"n":"CSWE_ENTRY_LEVEL","d":"The Certificates in Spoken and Written English level a client was placed at when they were first assessed, held once on the client profile.","full":"The Certificates in Spoken and Written English level a client was placed at when they were first assessed, held once on the client profile. CSWE runs Preliminary, Certificate I, Certificate II and Certificate III, and the evaluation notes that Certificate III is \"the highest level obtainable in the AMEP\". The value is a placement judgement made at the start of tuition, so it is the closest thing the file has to a baseline English level under the pre-2017 curriculum.","dsrc":"Department of Home Affairs, Evaluation of the Adult Migrant English Program New Business Model (Social Compass, 2019)","durl":"https://immi.homeaffairs.gov.au/amep-subsite/Files/amep-evalution-new-business-model.pdf","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"CSWE level attained in entry assessment","k":"CSWE certificate level assigned at entry assessment","def":"A CSWE certificate level. The four levels carry very different expected workloads: 210 to 660 supervised hours for Preliminary and 370 to 630 for Certificate III, with 1,415 to 2,430 supervised hours to move from beginner to Certificate III.","p":"2003 to 2019","s":"sourced","src":"Department of Home Affairs, Evaluation of the Adult Migrant English Program New Business Model (Social Compass, 2019)","url":"https://immi.homeaffairs.gov.au/amep-subsite/Files/amep-evalution-new-business-model.pdf","lim":"An entry level is not an award. The client has been placed at that level, not certified at it, and amep_csweawards is the only place a granted certificate appears. Entry assessment also moved to the Australian Core Skills Framework for new clients from 1 July 2017, so this column thins out for later cohorts rather than recording a genuine absence of assessment.","where":["madipge-mig-d-amep-client-03-19 / amep_cltpro_dob_visa_treated"]},{"n":"CSWE_LEVEL","d":"The certificate level of a CSWE course, held once per award code on the AMEP award reference table.","full":"The certificate level of a CSWE course, held once per award code on the AMEP award reference table. CSWE was the curriculum taught across the whole AMEP under the contract before July 2017, and its levels are Preliminary, Certificate I, Certificate II and Certificate III. The column describes the course, so it becomes a statement about a person only after joining AWARD_CODE to amep_csweawards.","dsrc":"Department of Home Affairs, Evaluation of the Adult Migrant English Program New Business Model (Social Compass, 2019)","durl":"https://immi.homeaffairs.gov.au/amep-subsite/Files/amep-evalution-new-business-model.pdf","dp":"ai","vp":"ai","od":"Certificate level of CSWE award/course","k":"Certificate level of the CSWE course","def":"A CSWE certificate level attached to a course code. The reference table also carries the award name, description and accreditation year for the same code, so the level is one attribute of a course record rather than a client outcome.","p":"2003 to 2019","s":"sourced","src":"Department of Home Affairs, Evaluation of the Adult Migrant English Program New Business Model (Social Compass, 2019)","url":"https://immi.homeaffairs.gov.au/amep-subsite/Files/amep-evalution-new-business-model.pdf","lim":"The level is not scaled to the AMEP entitlement, and reading it as an achievable target misleads. Streaming began with the new business model on 1 July 2017 and has two values. The evaluation says \"Pre-Employment English is for those students who wish to participate in the workplace or further training and is mandatory for those referred to the AMEP by an employment services provider\", while Social English is for clients improving conversational English to live independently in their community. INITIAL_STREAM holds the stream first assigned, so the pair shows whether a client moved.","dsrc":"Department of Home Affairs, Evaluation of the Adult Migrant English Program New Business Model (Social Compass, 2019)","durl":"https://immi.homeaffairs.gov.au/amep-subsite/Files/amep-evalution-new-business-model.pdf","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Stream type at time of this reporting - prior to 01/07/19","k":"AMEP tuition stream at the reporting date","def":"A two-category stream classification introduced under the 2017 AMEP contract. Pre-Employment English must use a nationally accredited curriculum; Social English may use non-accredited material and has larger classes and lighter teacher qualification requirements.","p":"2003 to 2019","s":"sourced","src":"Department of Home Affairs, Evaluation of the Adult Migrant English Program New Business Model (Social Compass, 2019)","url":"https://immi.homeaffairs.gov.au/amep-subsite/Files/amep-evalution-new-business-model.pdf","lim":"A blank is not a data fault for anyone whose AMEP participation ended before 1 July 2017, because streams did not exist then. The split is also far from even: the evaluation reports 77 per cent of classes as Pre-Employment English, 5 per cent as Social English and 18 per cent blended. Centrelink mutual obligation requirements do force some clients into Pre-Employment English, but the evaluation finds only five per cent of students are in that position, so the imbalance is not explained by that referral pathway.","where":["madipge-mig-d-amep-client-03-19 / amep_cltpro_dob_visa_treated"]},{"n":"DATE_EXTRACTED","d":"The day Home Affairs pulled this AMEP table for delivery to the ABS, so it dates the snapshot rather than anything the client did.","full":"The day Home Affairs pulled this AMEP table for delivery to the ABS, so it dates the snapshot rather than anything the client did. Because each AMEP table was extracted on its own schedule, the value can differ between the hours, address, profile and assessment tables for the same person.","dsrc":"ABS, Person Level Integrated Data Asset (PLIDA)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/data-integration/integrated-data/person-level-integrated-data-asset-plida","dp":"ai","vp":"ai","od":"Date data was extracted","k":"Date the AMEP file was extracted","def":"A calendar date. The domain is open: any date on which the department produced the extract, which for the AMEP tables in PLIDA sits after the last quarter the hours columns cover.","p":"2003 to 2011, 2003 to 2019, 2011 to 2019","s":"sourced","src":"ABS, Person Level Integrated Data Asset (PLIDA)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/data-integration/integrated-data/person-level-integrated-data-asset-plida","lim":"It cannot be used as an end date for a client's participation. Distance Learning gives clients one-on-one classes with an AMEP teacher by phone or online rather than in a classroom, and every AMEP client is eligible for it even while attending face-to-face classes. It is open ended and takes any date within the client's AMEP participation; there is no code list and no companion end date on the same row.","p":"2003 to 2019","s":"sourced","src":"Department of Home Affairs, Evaluation of the Adult Migrant English Program New Business Model (Social Compass, 2019)","url":"https://immi.homeaffairs.gov.au/amep-subsite/Files/amep-evalution-new-business-model.pdf","lim":"A referral is not a commencement or a volume of study. Registration is an early event: an eligible migrant must register within six months of arrival, so the answer describes someone who has usually been in Australia only weeks or months. It sits alongside the other self-reported registration fields, OCCUPATION_AT_REGISTRATION, HIGHEST_QUAL_AT_REGISTRATION and YEARS_OF_SCHOOLING.","dsrc":"Department of Home Affairs, Evaluation of the Adult Migrant English Program New Business Model (Social Compass, 2019)","durl":"https://immi.homeaffairs.gov.au/amep-subsite/Files/amep-evalution-new-business-model.pdf","dp":"ai","vp":"ai","od":"Employment status at time of registration in AMEP (self reporting)","k":"Self-reported employment status at AMEP registration","def":"A short status code or label supplied by the client. The custodian publishes no code list for it and the field is not coded to the ABS labour force status classification, so the categories have to be read off the data.","p":"2003 to 2019","s":"sourced","src":"Department of Home Affairs, Evaluation of the Adult Migrant English Program New Business Model (Social Compass, 2019)","url":"https://immi.homeaffairs.gov.au/amep-subsite/Files/amep-evalution-new-business-model.pdf","lim":"It is not a labour force measure and will not agree with employment observed in tax or payroll data for the same person. Enrolment is a later step than registration: eligible clients \"must register with an AMEP service provider within six months of their arrival in Australia ... commence tuition within 12 months and finish within 5 years\", so this year can fall a year after arrival. It is the natural cohort variable for the file, because AMEP commencements, expenditure and retention are all reported by financial year.","dsrc":"Department of Home Affairs, Evaluation of the Adult Migrant English Program New Business Model (Social Compass, 2019)","durl":"https://immi.homeaffairs.gov.au/amep-subsite/Files/amep-evalution-new-business-model.pdf","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Client's first time of enrolment in (first attendance at) AMEP - financial year of","k":"Australian financial year of first AMEP enrolment","def":"An Australian financial year running 1 July to 30 June, written as a year or year pair. Enrolment dates matter administratively because the legislated timeframes and the 510-hour entitlement clock hang off them. It is one of three override flags on the client profile, beside REGISTRATION_DATE_OVERRIDE and ENTITLEMENT_DATE_OVERRIDE.","dsrc":"Department of Home Affairs, Evaluation of the Adult Migrant English Program New Business Model (Social Compass, 2019)","durl":"https://immi.homeaffairs.gov.au/amep-subsite/Files/amep-evalution-new-business-model.pdf","dp":"ai","vp":"ai","od":"Whether INITIAL ENROLMENT DATE has been overrided through overrides process","k":"Indicator that the initial enrolment date was set by the overrides process","def":"A two-state indicator, set or not set. It describes how the neighbouring date was arrived at, not what the date is, and no code list for the flag is published.","p":"2003 to 2019","s":"sourced","src":"Department of Home Affairs, Evaluation of the Adult Migrant English Program New Business Model (Social Compass, 2019)","url":"https://immi.homeaffairs.gov.au/amep-subsite/Files/amep-evalution-new-business-model.pdf","lim":"It does not record the original date, the reason for the change or who made it, so it cannot support any analysis of why enrolment dates move. Read the two columns together: the flag is the only signal that the deadline on the row is an administrative decision rather than the standard calculation.","dsrc":"Department of Home Affairs, Evaluation of the Adult Migrant English Program New Business Model (Social Compass, 2019)","durl":"https://immi.homeaffairs.gov.au/amep-subsite/Files/amep-evalution-new-business-model.pdf","dp":"ai","vp":"ai","od":"Whether ENTITLEMENT END DATE has been overrided through overrides process","k":"Indicator that the entitlement end date was set by the overrides process","def":"A two-state indicator, set or not set. The ninth code is not a state: the ABS puts \"Jervis Bay Territory, and the Territories of Christmas Island, Cocos (Keeling) Islands and Norfolk Island ... as one spatial unit at the State and Territory level under the category of Other Territories\". The column's own metadata has no description, only the name repeated, so the ASGS edition has to be read from the sibling geography columns.","dsrc":"Australian Bureau of Statistics, Australian Statistical Geography Standard (ASGS): Volume 1 - Main Structure and Greater Capital City Statistical Areas, July 2016, Australia (AUS) and State | Territory (S|T)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/by%20Subject/1270.0.55.001~July%202016~Main%20Features~Australia%20(AUS)%20and%20State%20%7C%20Territory%20(S%7CT)~10017","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"FIRST_TRAIN_SITE_STATE_ASGS_2016","k":"State and territory code, ASGS 2016","def":"A single digit: 1 New South Wales, 2 Victoria, 3 Queensland, 4 South Australia, 5 Western Australia, 6 Tasmania, 7 Northern Territory, 8 Australian Capital Territory, 9 Other Territories.","p":"2003 to 2019","s":"sourced","src":"Australian Bureau of Statistics, Australian Statistical Geography Standard (ASGS): Volume 1 - Main Structure and Greater Capital City Statistical Areas, July 2016, Australia (AUS) and State | Territory (S|T)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/by%20Subject/1270.0.55.001~July%202016~Main%20Features~Australia%20(AUS)%20and%20State%20%7C%20Territory%20(S%7CT)~10017","lim":"It is not the client's state of residence and not a settlement destination. A client who registered in one state and first attended in another shows the second here while REGISTRATION_STATE_ASGS_2016 shows the first, and a state total built from this column counts provider locations rather than migrants.","where":["madipge-mig-d-amep-address-03-19 / amep_address_2003_19"]},{"n":"GENDER","d":"The client's gender as recorded in ARMS when they registered with the AMEP, held once on the client profile rather than per event.","full":"The client's gender as recorded in ARMS when they registered with the AMEP, held once on the client profile rather than per event. The ABS standard treats this as a distinct concept from sex: \"Gender is a social and cultural concept. It is about social and cultural differences in identity, expression and experience as a man, woman or non-binary person.\" The AMEP collection long predates that standard, so the categories in the data are the program's own operational ones and no code list is published with the data item list.","dsrc":"Australian Bureau of Statistics, Standard for Sex, Gender, Variations of Sex Characteristics and Sexual Orientation Variables","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/standards/standard-sex-gender-variations-sex-characteristics-and-sexual-orientation-variables/latest-release","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Client's gender","k":"Client's recorded gender","def":"A short code or label for gender, one value per client, entered at registration by a provider rather than derived. The domain is not published, so the categories present have to be read off the data.","p":"2003 to 2019","s":"sourced","src":"Australian Bureau of Statistics, Standard for Sex, Gender, Variations of Sex Characteristics and Sexual Orientation Variables","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/standards/standard-sex-gender-variations-sex-characteristics-and-sexual-orientation-variables/latest-release","lim":"It cannot be lined up with an ABS gender variable without first checking the codes. A field of this age usually offers two categories and an unknown, so an apparently zero non-binary count is evidence about the registration form and not about the client population.","where":["madipge-mig-d-amep-client-03-19 / amep_cltpro_dob_visa_treated"]},{"n":"HEARD_ABOUT_AMEP_FROM","d":"How the client says they came to hear about the AMEP, captured once at registration.","full":"How the client says they came to hear about the AMEP, captured once at registration. It is an outreach field rather than an eligibility one: Home Affairs promotes the program through providers, settlement services, employment services and a flyer published in many languages, and this column records which of those routes the client named. It sits with REGISTRATION_CENTRE and REGISTRATION_DATE, so it describes the moment of registration and not the moment of first attendance.","dsrc":"Department of Home Affairs, Adult Migrant English Program - About the program","durl":"https://immi.homeaffairs.gov.au/settling-in-australia/amep/about-the-program","dp":"ai","vp":"ai","od":"Where client heard about AMEP from","k":"Referral source reported at registration","def":"A coded referral source, one value per client, with no code list published in the PLIDA data item list or on the department's AMEP pages.","p":"2003 to 2019","s":"sourced","src":"Department of Home Affairs, Adult Migrant English Program - About the program","url":"https://immi.homeaffairs.gov.au/settling-in-australia/amep/about-the-program","lim":"It cannot measure what caused a person to enrol. Several routes usually apply at once, the answer is what the client recalled and what the officer coded, and a client registering again after an earlier spell may name the provider they already knew rather than the source that first reached them.","where":["madipge-mig-d-amep-client-03-19 / amep_cltpro_dob_visa_treated"]},{"n":"HIGHEST_QUAL_AT_REGISTRATION","d":"The highest qualification the client said they held when they registered with the AMEP, taken from self-report and not verified.","full":"The highest qualification the client said they held when they registered with the AMEP, taken from self-report and not verified. It covers overseas study as well as Australian, which is the point of collecting it, because a client with a foreign degree and no English is a different teaching problem from one with little schooling. YEARS_OF_SCHOOLING and YEARS_OF_TERTIARY_STUDY on the same row hold the duration side of the same self-report, and OCCUPATION_PRE_MIGRATION the work side.","dsrc":"Australian Bureau of Statistics, Australian Standard Classification of Education (ASCED), 2001","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/classifications/australian-standard-classification-education-asced/latest-release","dp":"ai","vp":"ai","od":"Highest qualification at time of registration with AMEP (self reporting)","k":"Self-reported highest qualification at registration","def":"A coded qualification level, one value per client. The ABS publishes ASCED as the national standard for classifying attainment by level and field, but the data item list does not say the AMEP field is coded to it.","p":"2003 to 2019","s":"sourced","src":"Australian Bureau of Statistics, Australian Standard Classification of Education (ASCED), 2001","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/classifications/australian-standard-classification-education-asced/latest-release","lim":"It will not line up with Census or ASCED attainment data unless you build the mapping yourself, and it is frozen at registration, so a qualification completed in Australia after enrolment never appears and an upward move over a client's AMEP years is invisible.","where":["madipge-mig-d-amep-client-03-19 / amep_cltpro_dob_visa_treated"]},{"n":"HTS_2011_Q3","d":"Hours of Home Tutor Scheme tuition the client attended in the July to September quarter of 2011, the column named HTS_2011_Q3.","full":"Hours of Home Tutor Scheme tuition the client attended in the July to September quarter of 2011, the column named HTS_2011_Q3. HTS is the AMEP's volunteer tutor sub-program, the one-to-one scheme the ANAO records as the Home Tutor Scheme and later the Volunteer Tutor Scheme, and this column holds one quarter of it. A person's whole history runs across the 32 HTS columns of amep_clientshours_2011_19, not down the rows. A July to September column opens the financial year, which is when contract and funding changes take effect. This is the opening year of the wide file: the earlier table amep_clientshours_2003_11 carries no HTS series at all, only AMEP, AMEPDL, SLPT, SPP and SPPDL in yearly columns, so quarterly Home Tutor Scheme hours start here, with the program then run by the Department of Immigration and Citizenship under the 2011 AMEP contracts.","dsrc":"Australian National Audit Office, performance audit 'Administration of the Adult Migrant English Program Contracts'","durl":"https://www.anao.gov.au/work/performance-audit/administration-the-adult-migrant-english-program-contracts","dp":"ai","vp":"ai","od":"HTS - number of hours attended by client in 2011 Quarter 3","k":"Home Tutor Scheme hours attended, July to September 2011","def":"A count of hours attended in the one quarter named in the column, held as a number with the client on the row. There is no code list: a zero, a whole or part-hour total and an empty cell are all possible, and the 32 HTS columns together span 1 July 2011 to 30 June 2019.","p":"2011 to 2019","s":"sourced","src":"Australian National Audit Office, performance audit 'Administration of the Adult Migrant English Program Contracts'","url":"https://www.anao.gov.au/work/performance-audit/administration-the-adult-migrant-english-program-contracts","lim":"An empty cell does not mean the client wanted no tutoring. A client not yet registered, already exited, or waiting for a tutor match all leave the same blank as one who was enrolled and attended nothing, and the column carries no enrolment flag to separate them.","where":["madipge-mig-d-amep-activity-11-19 / amep_clientshours_2011_19"]},{"n":"HTS_2011_Q4","d":"Hours of Home Tutor Scheme tuition the client attended in the October to December quarter of 2011, the column named HTS_2011_Q4.","full":"Hours of Home Tutor Scheme tuition the client attended in the October to December quarter of 2011, the column named HTS_2011_Q4. The measure is hours attended under the volunteer one-to-one tutor scheme, run alongside classroom tuition. It is stored wide: the client is the row and the quarter is the column name, so a series is read across the table rather than down it. An October to December column runs up to the end-of-year break. This is the opening year of the wide file: the earlier table amep_clientshours_2003_11 carries no HTS series at all, only AMEP, AMEPDL, SLPT, SPP and SPPDL in yearly columns, so quarterly Home Tutor Scheme hours start here, with the program then run by the Department of Immigration and Citizenship under the 2011 AMEP contracts.","dsrc":"Australian National Audit Office, performance audit 'Administration of the Adult Migrant English Program Contracts'","durl":"https://www.anao.gov.au/work/performance-audit/administration-the-adult-migrant-english-program-contracts","dp":"ai","vp":"ai","od":"HTS - number of hours attended by client in 2011 Quarter 4","k":"Home Tutor Scheme hours attended, October to December 2011","def":"A count of hours attended in the one quarter named in the column, held as a number with the client on the row. There is no code list: a zero, a whole or part-hour total and an empty cell are all possible, and the 32 HTS columns together span 1 July 2011 to 30 June 2019.","p":"2011 to 2019","s":"sourced","src":"Australian National Audit Office, performance audit 'Administration of the Adult Migrant English Program Contracts'","url":"https://www.anao.gov.au/work/performance-audit/administration-the-adult-migrant-english-program-contracts","lim":"Hours with a volunteer are not hours of teaching. The tutor is not an AMEP teacher and the scheme is not assessed, so this column cannot support a claim about tuition quality or about progress on the ACSF or a CSWE certificate.","where":["madipge-mig-d-amep-activity-11-19 / amep_clientshours_2011_19"]},{"n":"HTS_2012_Q1","d":"Hours of Home Tutor Scheme tuition the client attended in the January to March quarter of 2012, the column named HTS_2012_Q1.","full":"Hours of Home Tutor Scheme tuition the client attended in the January to March quarter of 2012, the column named HTS_2012_Q1. This counts attended hours of volunteer home tutoring, sitting beside the AMEP, AMEPDL, SPP, SPPDL, SLPT and CHILDCARE columns that measure the other AMEP activities for the same quarter. Each client has one row, so their tutoring history is spread across columns. A January to March column covers the start of the teaching year, after the December and January break. The whole of 2012 sits inside the 2011 contract period under one department, which makes its four columns the cleanest run of comparable quarters in the file.","dsrc":"Australian National Audit Office, performance audit 'Administration of the Adult Migrant English Program Contracts'","durl":"https://www.anao.gov.au/work/performance-audit/administration-the-adult-migrant-english-program-contracts","dp":"ai","vp":"ai","od":"HTS - number of hours attended by client in 2012 Quarter 1","k":"Home Tutor Scheme hours attended, January to March 2012","def":"A count of hours attended in the one quarter named in the column, held as a number with the client on the row. There is no code list: a zero, a whole or part-hour total and an empty cell are all possible, and the 32 HTS columns together span 1 July 2011 to 30 June 2019.","p":"2011 to 2019","s":"sourced","src":"Australian National Audit Office, performance audit 'Administration of the Adult Migrant English Program Contracts'","url":"https://www.anao.gov.au/work/performance-audit/administration-the-adult-migrant-english-program-contracts","lim":"These are not entitlement hours. ARMS is the \"AMEP Reporting Management System\", the departmental record store the ANAO describes as the program's legacy system, and amep_csweawardsrefcodes is its lookup list of CSWE awards. Each row pairs this identifier with AWARD_CODE, AWARD_NAME, AWARD_DESCRIPTION, CSWE_LEVEL and CSWE_ACCREDITATION_YEAR, which makes the table the decoder for AWARD_CODE in amep_csweawards.","dsrc":"Australian National Audit Office, performance audit 'Administration of the Adult Migrant English Program Contracts'","durl":"https://www.anao.gov.au/work/performance-audit/administration-the-adult-migrant-english-program-contracts","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"ARMS ID for CSWE award/course","k":"ARMS row identifier for a CSWE award or course","def":"A surrogate identifier that is unique within the reference table, with no meaning outside ARMS and no relation to the certificate's national course code.","p":"2003 to 2019","s":"sourced","src":"Australian National Audit Office, performance audit 'Administration of the Adult Migrant English Program Contracts'","url":"https://www.anao.gov.au/work/performance-audit/administration-the-adult-migrant-english-program-contracts","lim":"It is not the join key. amep_csweawards carries AWARD_CODE and not this identifier, so a join on ID quietly returns nothing, and because a certificate re-accredited in a later year takes a new reference row, one qualification can appear several times under different identifiers.","where":["madipge-mig-d-amep-award-codes-03-19 / amep_csweawardsrefcodes"]},{"n":"INITIAL_ACSF_ASSESSMENT_DATE","d":"The day the client's first Australian Core Skills Framework assessment was done, recorded for clients new to the AMEP from 1 July 2017.","full":"The day the client's first Australian Core Skills Framework assessment was done, recorded for clients new to the AMEP from 1 July 2017. It dates the INITIAL_ ACSF indicator columns on the same row, while LATEST_ACSF_ASSESSMENT_DATE marks the other end of the client's assessed progress.","dsrc":"Department of Employment and Workplace Relations, Australian Core Skills Framework","durl":"https://www.dewr.gov.au/foundation-skills/australian-core-skills-framework-acsf","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Date when initial ACSF assessment was conducted - under contract from 1 July 2017 for new clients only","k":"Date of first ACSF assessment","def":"A calendar date, one value per client, present only where an ACSF assessment was recorded, so in practice from 1 July 2017 onwards.","p":"2003 to 2019","s":"sourced","src":"Department of Employment and Workplace Relations, Australian Core Skills Framework","url":"https://www.dewr.gov.au/foundation-skills/australian-core-skills-framework-acsf","lim":"A blank does not mean the client was never assessed. The gap between arrival and INITIAL_ENROLMENT_DATE is the quantity worth building, because it measures how long a migrant waited before starting English tuition.","dsrc":"Department of Home Affairs, Adult Migrant English Program - About the program","durl":"https://immi.homeaffairs.gov.au/settling-in-australia/amep/about-the-program","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Visa information - Client's initial arrival date in Australia","k":"Date of first arrival in Australia","def":"A calendar date, one value per client, sourced from departmental records and grouped with the other visa fields on amep_cltpro_dob_visa_treated.","p":"2003 to 2019","s":"sourced","src":"Department of Home Affairs, Adult Migrant English Program - About the program","url":"https://immi.homeaffairs.gov.au/settling-in-australia/amep/about-the-program","lim":"It is a first arrival, not the arrival that led to settlement. The scale's publisher describes it as \"a detailed scale that describes real-life language behaviour at 12 levels from zero to native-like proficiency\", assessed in an interview rather than a written test. LATEST_ASLPR_DATE dates the matching LATEST_ ratings, so the two dates bound whatever progress the pair of assessments shows.","dsrc":"ISLPR Language Services, 'Summary of ISLPR | Marking Criteria'","durl":"https://islpr.org/why-use-islpr/summary-of-islpr","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Date of initial ASLPR assessment","k":"Date of first ASLPR assessment","def":"A calendar date, one value per client, present only where an ASLPR assessment was recorded. INITIAL_ASLPR_DATE dates it and LATEST_ASLPR_LISTEN holds the same rating at the client's most recent assessment.","dsrc":"D. E. INITIAL_LEARNING_01 holds the other learning indicator, and the AMEP file carries no numeracy indicators, .09 to .11, because the program teaches English.","dsrc":"Department of Employment and Workplace Relations, Australian Core Skills Framework (full framework, Table 3: ACSF Performance Indicators)","durl":"https://www.dewr.gov.au/download/6976/australian-core-skills-framework/10893/australian-core-skills-framework/pdf","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Initial ACSF assessment - Learning .02","k":"ACSF level on learning indicator .02","def":"An ACSF level: Pre Level 1, which the framework covers in a separate supplement that is not organised against Indicators, or a whole level on the framework's \"five levels of performance ranging from 1 (low level performance) to 5 (high level performance)\". The suffix in the column name is the indicator number and not a level, because the ACSF has \"11 Indicators; two each for Learning, Reading, Writing and Oral Communication and three for Numeracy\". INITIAL_ORAL_COMMUNICATION_08 holds the other oral communication indicator, and the AMEP file carries no numeracy indicators, .09 to .11, because the program teaches English.","dsrc":"Department of Employment and Workplace Relations, Australian Core Skills Framework (full framework, Table 3: ACSF Performance Indicators)","durl":"https://www.dewr.gov.au/download/6976/australian-core-skills-framework/10893/australian-core-skills-framework/pdf","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Initial ACSF assessment - Oral communication .07","k":"ACSF level on oral communication indicator .07","def":"An ACSF level: Pre Level 1, which the framework covers in a separate supplement that is not organised against Indicators, or a whole level on the framework's \"five levels of performance ranging from 1 (low level performance) to 5 (high level performance)\". The suffix in the column name is the indicator number and not a level, because the ACSF has \"11 Indicators; two each for Learning, Reading, Writing and Oral Communication and three for Numeracy\". INITIAL_ORAL_COMMUNICATION_07 holds the other oral communication indicator, and the AMEP file carries no numeracy indicators, .09 to .11, because the program teaches English.","dsrc":"Department of Employment and Workplace Relations, Australian Core Skills Framework (full framework, Table 3: ACSF Performance Indicators)","durl":"https://www.dewr.gov.au/download/6976/australian-core-skills-framework/10893/australian-core-skills-framework/pdf","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Initial ACSF assessment - Oral communication .08","k":"ACSF level on oral communication indicator .08","def":"An ACSF level: Pre Level 1, which the framework covers in a separate supplement that is not organised against Indicators, or a whole level on the framework's \"five levels of performance ranging from 1 (low level performance) to 5 (high level performance)\". The framework writes level and indicator together, so a client at level 1 on oral communication has achieved both 1.07 and 1.08.","p":"2003 to 2019","s":"sourced","src":"Department of Employment and Workplace Relations, Australian Core Skills Framework (full framework, Table 3: ACSF Performance Indicators)","url":"https://www.dewr.gov.au/download/6976/australian-core-skills-framework/10893/australian-core-skills-framework/pdf","lim":"A listening rating cannot stand in for oral communication as a whole.
