A client between plans, waiting for materials or paused for illness looks the same in this cell as one who never took up distance learning. And it cannot be compared directly with the 2003 to 2011 annual columns, because a quarter and a year are different denominators.","where":["madipge-mig-d-amep-activity-11-19 / amep_clientshours_2011_19"]},{"n":"SPPDL_2012_Q2","d":"Hours of Special Preparatory Program tuition this client took by distance learning in the quarter AMEP labels 2012 Quarter 2.","full":"Hours of Special Preparatory Program tuition this client took by distance learning in the quarter AMEP labels 2012 Quarter 2. By this point the entitlement was the pair of tiers the evaluation records, after \"the SPP was expanded to allow 400 additional hours of AMEP tuition to humanitarian entrants between 16 and 24 years of age who had less than seven years of schooling\" in 2004. This quarter sits a year ahead of the AMEP contract that ran from July 2013 to June 2017, so it rests on the oldest arrangements in the quarterly table. Each client has one row and each quarter one column, so a person's distance learning series is read across columns and totalled by adding them.","dsrc":"Department of Home Affairs, Evaluation of the Adult Migrant English Program New Business Model (Social Compass, August 2019)","durl":"https://immi.homeaffairs.gov.au/amep-subsite/Files/amep-evalution-new-business-model.pdf","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"SPPDL - number of hours attended by client in 2012 Quarter 2","k":"Special Preparatory Program distance learning hours in the quarter","def":"A count of hours, held as a number rather than a coded category, so zero, a part hour and several hundred are all in range. The domain is set by the entitlement the evaluation tabulates: 400 additional hours for a humanitarian entrant under 25 with seven years of schooling or less, and 100 hours for one under 25 with eight years or more and for anyone aged 25 and over. The rule that a client within 50 km of a delivery site may use only half of their SPP hours in distance learning is documented for the contract from July 2017, not for this quarter.","p":"2011 to 2019","s":"sourced","src":"Department of Home Affairs, Evaluation of the Adult Migrant English Program New Business Model (Social Compass, August 2019)","url":"https://immi.homeaffairs.gov.au/amep-subsite/Files/amep-evalution-new-business-model.pdf","lim":"It does not identify the provider or the delivery arrangement behind the hours, so a step between quarters can be a change in how a consortium member recorded study rather than a change in the client. It also records no reason for studying at a distance, so remoteness, work, illness and carer duties all read alike.","where":["madipge-mig-d-amep-activity-11-19 / amep_clientshours_2011_19"]},{"n":"SPPDL_2012_Q3","d":"Hours of Special Preparatory Program tuition this client took by distance learning in the quarter AMEP labels 2012 Quarter 3.","full":"Hours of Special Preparatory Program tuition this client took by distance learning in the quarter AMEP labels 2012 Quarter 3. The department's 2019 evaluation describes the mode as it stood at that report: \"DL students have one-on-one classes with an AMEP teacher via Skype or telephone, and do self-paced study using online materials or books and CDs.\" The entitlement in this quarter is the two tiers settled in 2004, and the funding cap on the subprogram had not yet been removed. This is one cell of a wide quarterly series; the period sits in the column name, so rows cannot be grouped by it.","dsrc":"Department of Home Affairs, Evaluation of the Adult Migrant English Program New Business Model (Social Compass, August 2019)","durl":"https://immi.homeaffairs.gov.au/amep-subsite/Files/amep-evalution-new-business-model.pdf","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"SPPDL - number of hours attended by client in 2012 Quarter 3","k":"Special Preparatory Program distance learning hours in the quarter","def":"The cell holds hours, not a code. Any non-negative number is admissible and there is no residual or not-stated category. Its ceiling is the SPP entitlement table: 100 additional hours for a client under 25 with eight or more years of schooling, 400 for one under 25 with seven years or less, and 100 for a client aged 25 or over. How many entitlement hours a week of distance study consumed is documented only for the July 2013 contract onwards, so it cannot be assumed for this quarter.","p":"2011 to 2019","s":"sourced","src":"Department of Home Affairs, Evaluation of the Adult Migrant English Program New Business Model (Social Compass, August 2019)","url":"https://immi.homeaffairs.gov.au/amep-subsite/Files/amep-evalution-new-business-model.pdf","lim":"It is not observed teaching time. The evaluation describes distance learning under the contract from July 2013, when \"students had five hours deducted from their entitlement each week\", only one of which was taught; it publishes no equivalent rule for this period, so how much of the figure was taught and how much was self-paced is unknown. It also says nothing about the later rule, recorded for the contract from July 2017, that \"SPP clients who live within 50 km of an AMEP delivery site may only use half of their allocated SPP hours in DL\"; no such restriction is documented for this quarter, so the column's meaning is not constant along the panel.","where":["madipge-mig-d-amep-activity-11-19 / amep_clientshours_2011_19"]},{"n":"SPPDL_2012_Q4","d":"Hours of Special Preparatory Program tuition this client took by distance learning in the quarter AMEP labels 2012 Quarter 4.","full":"Hours of Special Preparatory Program tuition this client took by distance learning in the quarter AMEP labels 2012 Quarter 4. Distance learning runs alongside classes rather than instead of them: \"All students are eligible for DL, even if they are attending classroom-based tuition.\" This quarter closes 2012 under consortium delivery, and the 2019 evaluation does not reach it: its client extract starts on 1 July 2013. The table is wide rather than long, so setting this quarter beside the next means comparing two columns of the same row.","dsrc":"Department of Home Affairs, Evaluation of the Adult Migrant English Program New Business Model (Social Compass, August 2019)","durl":"https://immi.homeaffairs.gov.au/amep-subsite/Files/amep-evalution-new-business-model.pdf","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"SPPDL - number of hours attended by client in 2012 Quarter 4","k":"Special Preparatory Program distance learning hours in the quarter","def":"Hours are stored as a numeric quantity, so there is no code list to decode and the domain is bounded by entitlement rather than by a set of labels. What bounds the number is the evaluation's entitlement table, which gives 400 additional hours only to an under-25 humanitarian entrant with seven years of schooling or less and 100 hours in the other two cases. Consortium delivery means several providers stood behind these hours, so the recording practice behind the number was not uniform.","p":"2011 to 2019","s":"sourced","src":"Department of Home Affairs, Evaluation of the Adult Migrant English Program New Business Model (Social Compass, August 2019)","url":"https://immi.homeaffairs.gov.au/amep-subsite/Files/amep-evalution-new-business-model.pdf","lim":"A zero cannot be read as a client who preferred a classroom. The subprogram behind the hours \"provides refugee and humanitarian entrants with additional hours of English language tuition in the AMEP\", and this column is the part of those additional hours taken at a distance. This quarter falls in the first half of 2013, before the contract that began that July, so it lies outside the client data the 2019 evaluation analysed. The hours table carries one column per quarter, so a client's distance learning history runs across the row rather than down it.","dsrc":"Department of Home Affairs, Evaluation of the Adult Migrant English Program New Business Model (Social Compass, August 2019)","durl":"https://immi.homeaffairs.gov.au/amep-subsite/Files/amep-evalution-new-business-model.pdf","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"SPPDL - number of hours attended by client in 2013 Quarter 1","k":"Special Preparatory Program distance learning hours in the quarter","def":"This is a numeric quantity of hours. The classification behind it is the two-tier SPP entitlement, 100 or 400 additional hours according to the client's age and years of prior schooling. This quarter ends before the July 2013 contract, so it is the last one recorded under the arrangements that contract replaced.","p":"2011 to 2019","s":"sourced","src":"Department of Home Affairs, Evaluation of the Adult Migrant English Program New Business Model (Social Compass, August 2019)","url":"https://immi.homeaffairs.gov.au/amep-subsite/Files/amep-evalution-new-business-model.pdf","lim":"It cannot show whether a client had a plan at all. The Special Preparatory Program is the extra English tuition offered to refugee and humanitarian entrants on top of the standard AMEP entitlement, and the DL in the name marks the hours taken by distance learning rather than in a classroom, which SPP_2013_Q2 holds. The quarter falls in the closing months of 2012-13, just before the July 2013 start of the participation series the department's evaluation reports on. The client is one row and the measure runs across the columns, so a distance-learning history is read left to right from SPPDL_2011_Q3 to SPPDL_2019_Q2 rather than down the rows.","dsrc":"Social Compass, Evaluation of the Adult Migrant English Program New Business Model, for the Department of Home Affairs, August 2019","durl":"https://immi.homeaffairs.gov.au/amep-subsite/Files/amep-evalution-new-business-model.pdf","dp":"ai","vp":"ai","od":"SPPDL - number of hours attended by client in 2013 Quarter 2","k":"Special Preparatory Program distance-learning hours attended, 2013 Q2","def":"A count of tuition hours attended, carried as a number rather than a code, for one delivery mode of one AMEP subprogram in one quarter. The classification behind the column family is the AMEP's own program structure: general AMEP tuition, AMEPDL, SPP, SPPDL, SLPT, HTS and CHILDCARE each carry a 32-column quarterly series in amep_clientshours_2011_19 running from 2011 Q3 to 2019 Q2, and EXTEND carries eight columns from 2017 Q3. Hours are entered by the AMEP service provider in the AMEP Reporting and Management System (ARMS) and summed to the quarter. For 2013 Q2 seven of those eight families carry a column, EXTEND excepted.","p":"2011 to 2019","s":"sourced","src":"Social Compass, Evaluation of the Adult Migrant English Program New Business Model, for the Department of Home Affairs, August 2019","url":"https://immi.homeaffairs.gov.au/amep-subsite/Files/amep-evalution-new-business-model.pdf","lim":"A zero or an empty cell does not mean the client did no remote SPP study that quarter. What is counted is also session time as the provider recorded it: the evaluation notes that ARMS \"only records full session attendance and approved absences\", with late arrivals, early departures and unapproved absences handled on spreadsheets outside the system, and the department measured an average 2.8 per cent gap between scheduled and actual attendance. AMEP Extend did not exist in this quarter: the department introduced it on 1 July 2017, so for 2012-13 no column in the table records tuition given to a client who reached 510 hours without the English they needed. It carries the same value on all six AMEP tables, so hours in 2003-11, hours in 2011-19, addresses, the client profile, CSWE awards and English proficiency assemble into one learner history, while AMET_CLNT_ID is the department's own client number inside its reporting system. In the live asset the equivalent key comes from the ABS Person Linkage Spine, which \"allows us to link datasets through a spine of key information, separate from the main body of data\"; in fplida the value is generated and means nothing outside this package.","dsrc":"ABS, Person Level Integrated Data Asset (PLIDA)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/data-integration/integrated-data/person-level-integrated-data-asset-plida","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Synthetic id of individual person on dataset","k":"Synthetic person-level identifier","def":"An opaque person-level identifier, one value per person, repeated on every row that belongs to that person. A client with two registrations, a break in tuition, a change of provider or several award records keeps one identifier, so counting rows counts episodes; deduplicate before treating a count as a headcount. It also cannot be joined to anything outside the asset, and a client who did not link to the spine is missing from the AMEP tables altogether rather than sitting in them with a blank key, which biases coverage rather than adding noise.","where":["madipge-mig-d-amep-activity-03-11 / amep_clientshours_2003_11","madipge-mig-d-amep-activity-11-19 / amep_clientshours_2011_19","madipge-mig-d-amep-address-03-19 / amep_address_2003_19","madipge-mig-d-amep-awards-03-19 / amep_csweawards","madipge-mig-d-amep-client-03-19 / amep_cltpro_dob_visa_treated","madipge-mig-d-amep-english-03-19 / amep_englishproficiency"]},{"n":"VISA_MIGRATION_CATEGORY","d":"The migration stream of the visa that made this client eligible for the AMEP, set once at registration.","full":"The migration stream of the visa that made this client eligible for the AMEP, set once at registration. It is the level above the subclass: the ABS groups the same Home Affairs codes the same way, noting that \"visa subclass (3-digit) information is then aggregated into visa streams (highest-level grouping) to produce the Skilled, Family, Humanitarian, Other and undetermined, and Total permanent groupings\". The category is also what opens or closes the Special Preparatory Program, whose hours sit in the SPP and SPPDL columns of the hours tables, because the SPP is for refugee and humanitarian entrants.","dsrc":"ABS, Migrant settlement outcomes methodology, 2023","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/methodologies/migrant-settlement-outcomes-methodology/2023","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Visa information - Client's visa migration category","k":"Migration stream of the client's AMEP-eligible visa","def":"A stream-level category rather than a list of visas, sitting above the subclass number in VISA_SUBCLASS and the subclass name in VISA_SUBCLASS_DESC on the same row. The streams that carry AMEP eligibility are the humanitarian, family and skilled streams.","p":"2003 to 2019","s":"sourced","src":"ABS, Migrant settlement outcomes methodology, 2023","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/methodologies/migrant-settlement-outcomes-methodology/2023","lim":"It is a stream at one moment, not a migration history. A person who arrived on a temporary visa and later became a permanent resident carries a single category here, and someone who held a humanitarian visa earlier but registered on a family visa will not read as humanitarian at all. Nor does the category by itself decide AMEP access: eligibility also turns on having less than functional English and on the registration, commencement and completion deadlines that attach to the visa start date.","where":["madipge-mig-d-amep-client-03-19 / amep_cltpro_dob_visa_treated"]},{"n":"VISA_SUBCLASS","d":"The visa subclass held by the client of the Adult Migrant English Program.","full":"The visa subclass held by the client of the Adult Migrant English Program. A subclass is Home Affairs' three-digit identifier for a specific visa product, and here it is also an eligibility statement: entitlement to the program depends on visa type, so the subclass explains why a client is in the file at all. Humanitarian subclasses and family stream subclasses carry different entitlements to tuition hours.","dsrc":"Department of Home Affairs, visa list","durl":"https://immi.homeaffairs.gov.au/visas/getting-a-visa/visa-listing","dp":"ai","vp":"ai","od":"Visa information - Client's visa subclass code","k":"Home Affairs visa subclass code","def":"The domain is open, so no finite value list applies.","p":"2003 to 2019","s":"sourced","src":"Department of Home Affairs, visa list","url":"https://immi.homeaffairs.gov.au/visas/getting-a-visa/visa-listing","lim":"Home Affairs publishes the subclasses but not the code list used here, so the mapping is not confirmed. Home Affairs identifies every visa by a subclass number and a name, and its visa listing is the register of those pairs; this column carries the name half. It describes the visa that opened the client's tuition entitlement, not the visa or citizenship they hold now, and not the visa they were on during any particular quarter of tuition.","dsrc":"Department of Home Affairs, Visa listing","durl":"https://immi.homeaffairs.gov.au/visas/getting-a-visa/visa-listing","dp":"ai","vp":"ai","od":"Visa information - Client's visa subclass description","k":"Home Affairs visa subclass name","def":"Free text naming one visa subclass, one value per client. It also cannot tell you whether the visa was still in force, since AMEP tuition can run for years after the grant and no end date accompanies the name.","where":["madipge-mig-d-amep-client-03-19 / amep_cltpro_dob_visa_treated"]},{"n":"YEAR_OF_BIRTH","d":"The AMEP client's year of birth, held beside MONTH_OF_BIRTH and with no day of month anywhere in the table.","full":"The AMEP client's year of birth, held beside MONTH_OF_BIRTH and with no day of month anywhere in the table. The ABS describes the AMEP collection as \"Information on participants in the English language tuition program, including their visa type, course attendance and educational outcomes\", and this is the age anchor for that participant record. AGE_GROUP_AT_REGISTRATION on the same row is the department's own banding of the same fact, so the two will not always agree at the edges of a band.","dsrc":"ABS, PLIDA data and legislation","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/data-integration/integrated-data/person-level-integrated-data-asset-plida/plida-data-and-legislation","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Year of birth","k":"Year of birth (four digits)","def":"A four-digit calendar year, one value per client on the client profile table. Age at registration, at first enrolment or at a given quarterly hours column can only be bracketed to a year, and where age decides an entitlement this matters: the Special Preparatory Program splits at 25 years, so two clients born in the same year can fall on opposite sides of that line. Read beside the SPP and SPPDL hour columns, it is how you see which clients had the larger entitlement to draw on.","dsrc":"Social Compass, Evaluation of the Adult Migrant English Program New Business Model, for the Department of Home Affairs, August 2019","durl":"https://immi.homeaffairs.gov.au/amep-subsite/Files/amep-evalution-new-business-model.pdf","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Number of years of schooling (self reporting)","k":"Years of schooling, self reported","def":"A count of years, self reported, one value per client.
